records.geography: Six ASEAN countries; consumer survey estimates reported by the GSM Association
records.source_unit: GSMA ASEAN Consumer Scam Report 2026, covering Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam

victims_reporting.unit: percent of scam victims reporting the incident
victims_reporting.period: 2026 report; reported scam cases and institutional resolution

reported_cases_unresolved.unit: percent of reported scam cases remaining unresolved
reported_cases_unresolved.period: 2026 report; reported scam cases and institutional resolution

money_losing_victims_recovered_none.unit: percent of money-losing victims recovering none of their losses
money_losing_victims_recovered_none.period: 2026 report; previous 12 months; scam exposure and financial recovery

money_losing_victims_recovered_all.unit: percent of money-losing victims recovering all losses
money_losing_victims_recovered_all.period: 2026 report; previous 12 months; scam exposure and financial recovery

channel_trust_effect.value: Consumers with unresolved cases report lower trust in communications channels, digital platforms, and data sharing
channel_trust_effect.period: 2026 report; reported scam cases and institutional resolution

provider_switching.value: Consumers who experienced scams were more than twice as likely to switch accounts or service providers than consumers who had not been affected
provider_switching.period: 2026 report; scam channels, worry, and consumer switching

records.geography: Great Britain; BSA adult respondents, with service-performance comparisons primarily for England and historical NHS series
records.source_unit: National Centre for Social Research, British Social Attitudes 43, Waiting for treatment

policy_feedback.value: Funding, targets, staffing, choice, migration, social care, and productivity are linked to legitimacy only when they become visible as shorter waits and reachable service
policy_feedback.period: 1997-2010 versus 2024-2025; resources, productivity, and visible feedback

legitimacy_route.value: Public satisfaction can recover over years when system performance becomes visibly better, but post-pandemic legitimacy remains historically weak

waiting_as_hidden_price.value: Access time is experienced as a system cost and a visible test of whether public provision is reachable
waiting_as_hidden_price.period: 2023-2025; waiting as the dominant dissatisfaction route

quality_access_split.value: The public can remain more positive about care quality than about the time and route required to reach care
quality_access_split.period: 2010-2025; quality and access diverge across NHS services

independent_source_families: National Centre for Social Research / British Social Attitudes
next_action: Use the shared unresolved/recovery/trust vocabulary to acquire a genuinely comparable repeated measure before any backtest or promotion.
boundary: Independent publishers can challenge a mechanism without making unlike survey and case measures numerically comparable.
